objects.description: Wrapper around a PROJ PJ object and cached CRS characteristics to accelerate coordinate transformations and geodesic computations.
Ordinal selector for coordinate components: x, y, z, m. Used for operations like swapping ordinates.

objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory allocation routine used by liblwgeom.

objects.definition: typedef void* (*lwreallocator)(void *mem, size_t size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory reallocation routine.

objects.definition: typedef void (*lwfreeor)(void* mem);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory free routine.

objects.definition:

  __attribute__ (( format(printf, 1, 0) ));
objects.description: Function pointer type for logging/reporting callbacks (printf-style formatting).

objects.definition:
typedef void (*lwdebuglogger)(int level, const char* fmt, va_list ap)
  __attribute__ (( format(printf, 2,0) ));
objects.description: Function pointer type for debug logging callbacks (printf-style).

objects.definition: typedef void (lwinterrupt_callback)(void);
objects.description: Callback signature used for periodic interruption handling during long-running algorithms.

objects.description: Bitmask representing geometry flags (Z, M, geodetic, bbox, readonly, solid).
Variable-length byte buffer with a size header, similar to PostgreSQL varlena, used for textual/binary encodings (WKT/WKB/etc).
Affine transform coefficients and offsets for coordinate transformations applied to geometries.
3D axis-aligned bounding box with SRID.
General geometry bounding box with dimensionality flags and ranges for X/Y/Z/M.

objects.definition:
typedef struct
{
    double  a;  /* semimajor axis */
    double  b;  /* semiminor axis b = (a - fa) */
    double  f;  /* flattening f = (a-b)/a */
    double  e;  /* eccentricity (first) */
    double  e_sq;   /* eccentricity squared (first) e_sq = (a*a-b*b)/(a*a) */
    double  radius;  /* spherical average radius = (2*a+b)/3 */
    char    name[20];  /* name of ellipse */
}
SPHEROID;
objects.description: Ellipsoid (spheroid) parameters used for geodetic calculations.
2D point with double precision coordinates.
3D point (X,Y,Z).
3D point type equivalent to POINT3DZ in this header.
3D point where the third ordinate is measure (M).
4D point with X, Y, Z, and M ordinates.
Dynamic array of serialized point coordinates with dimensionality flags; core storage for geometry vertices.
Compact on-disk/in-memory serialization format for geometries, including SRID and flags, optionally with bbox.
Abstract base structure for all geometry types; holds common metadata (bbox, SRID, flags, type) and type-specific payload via data pointer.
Light-weight point geometry implementation storing a single vertex in a POINTARRAY.
Light-weight linestring geometry storing a sequence of vertices in a POINTARRAY.
Triangle surface primitive represented as a ring of points.
CircularString curve geometry storing control points for arcs.
Polygon geometry with an array of linear rings (outer + holes).
MultiPoint homogeneous collection.
MultiLineString homogeneous collection.
MultiPolygon homogeneous collection.
Generic geometry collection holding an array of LWGEOM pointers.
CompoundCurve-like collection combining linear and circular components.
CurvePolygon geometry with rings that can be linear or curved.
MultiCurve collection type.
MultiSurface collection type.
PolyhedralSurface collection of polygons.
Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN) as a collection of triangles.
Grid snapping specification including origins, cell sizes, and scales for XYZM dimensions.
Minimum bounding circle result: center (optional pointer to POINT2D) and radius.

typedef struct struct_lwgeom_parser_result
{
	const char *wkinput;        /* Copy of pointer to input WKT/WKB */

Enum describing the meaning of a tolerance value for curve linearization.
Flags controlling behavior of curve linearization (symmetry and angle retention).

functions.name: lwgeom_version
functions.description: Returns the liblwgeom version string. The returned pointer is to static storage and must not be freed.

functions.name: clamp_srid
functions.description: Validate and clamp an SRID to the accepted range. Raises a notice if adjusted and an error if out of bounds. Exact notice/error mechanism depends on the library build. Returns a valid SRID.
requirements: Input srid must be an integer; values outside allowed range trigger notice/exception behavior as documented by PostGIS.

functions.name: lwgeom_set_handlers
functions.signature: void lwgeom_set_handlers(lwallocator allocator, lwreallocator reallocator, lwfreeor freeor, lwreporter errorreporter, lwreporter noticereporter);
functions.description: Install custom memory allocation and reporting handlers used by liblwgeom.
requirements: All function pointers passed must be either valid callable pointers or NULL if not provided.
If provided, errorreporter and noticereporter must support printf-like varargs semantics as declared.

functions.name: lwgeom_set_debuglogger
functions.description: Install a custom debug logging callback for liblwgeom. The callback signature matches printf-style varargs.
requirements: If provided, the debuglogger callback must be callable for the lifetime it's used and respect the printf-like varargs contract.

functions.name: lwgeom_request_interrupt
functions.description: Request interruption of running liblwgeom operations. Safe to call from signal handlers. Interrupted functions will attempt to exit early; their return values are undefined and must be ignored by callers.
requirements: Callers must not rely on return values from interrupted operations; treat them as undefined.

functions.name: lwgeom_cancel_interrupt
functions.description: Cancel any prior interruption request set by lwgeom_request_interrupt.

functions.name: lwgeom_register_interrupt_callback
functions.description: Register a periodic callback invoked during long-running algorithms (primarily for WIN32 signal dispatch). Returns the previously registered callback.
requirements: Callback must be reentrant and fast; it may request interruption by calling lwgeom_request_interrupt.
The provided callback pointer must remain valid while registered.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwmpoly
functions.description: Attempt to cast a generic LWGEOM to an LWMPOLY (MultiPolygon). Returns NULL if the cast is illegal or the type does not match.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid pointer to an LWGEOM representing a multipolygon to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwmline
functions.description: Attempt to cast a generic LWGEOM to an LWMLINE (MultiLineString). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid LWGEOM of multilinstring type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwmpoint
functions.description: Attempt to cast a generic LWGEOM to an LWMPOINT (MultiPoint). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid LWGEOM of multipoint type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwcollection
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWCOLLECTION. Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a collection type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwpoly
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWPOLY (Polygon). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a polygon type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwline
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWLINE (LineString). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a linestring type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwcircstring
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWCIRCSTRING (CircularString). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a circularstring type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwcurvepoly
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWCURVEPOLY (CurvePolygon). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a curvepolygon type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwcompound
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWCOMPOUND (CompoundCurve). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a compound curve type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwpsurface
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWPSURFACE (PolyhedralSurface). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a polyhedral surface type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwtriangle
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWTRIANGLE (Triangle). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a triangle type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_lwtin
functions.description: Attempt to cast LWGEOM to LWTIN (TIN). Returns NULL if cast is illegal.
requirements: lwgeom must be a TIN type to succeed.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_multi
functions.description: Return a multi-geometry equivalent of the input if applicable (e.g., wrap single into multi). Always returns a geometry (may clone/convert).
requirements: Input must be a valid LWGEOM pointer.

functions.name: lwgeom_as_curve
functions.description: Return a curve representation of the input if applicable (e.g., linear to curved). Returns a geometry, converting as needed.
requirements: Input must be a valid LWGEOM pointer.

functions.name: lwtin_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWTIN to its LWGEOM supertype. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWTIN.

functions.name: lwtriangle_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWTRIANGLE to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWTRIANGLE.

functions.name: lwpsurface_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWPSURFACE to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWPSURFACE.

functions.name: lwmpoly_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWMPOLY to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWMPOLY.

functions.name: lwmline_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWMLINE to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWMLINE.

functions.name: lwmpoint_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWMPOINT to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWMPOINT.

functions.name: lwcollection_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWCOLLECTION to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWCOLLECTION.

functions.name: lwcircstring_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWCIRCSTRING to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWCIRCSTRING.

functions.name: lwcompound_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWCOMPOUND to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWCOMPOUND.

functions.name: lwcurvepoly_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWCURVEPOLY to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWCURVEPOLY.

functions.name: lwpoly_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWPOLY to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWPOLY.

functions.name: lwline_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWLINE to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWLINE.

functions.name: lwpoint_as_lwgeom
functions.description: Upcast an LWPOINT to LWGEOM. Always succeeds.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to an LWPOINT.

functions.name: lwcollection_add_lwgeom
functions.description: Append a geometry to a collection, reallocating as needed. Returns the (possibly reallocated) collection pointer.
requirements: col must be a valid modifiable collection.
geom must be a valid LWGEOM pointer.
Caller must use the returned pointer as the new collection, since the address may change.

functions.name: lwmpoint_add_lwpoint
functions.description: Append a LWPOINT to a MultiPoint, reallocating as needed. Returns possibly reallocated collection.
requirements: mobj must be a valid LWMPOINT.
obj must be a valid LWPOINT.
Caller must use the returned pointer as the new object as its address may change.

functions.name: lwmline_add_lwline
functions.description: Append an LWLINE to a MultiLineString, reallocating as needed. Returns possibly reallocated object.
requirements: mobj must be a valid LWMLINE.
obj must be a valid LWLINE.
Use returned pointer for subsequent access as address may change.

functions.name: lwmpoly_add_lwpoly
functions.description: Append an LWPOLY to a MultiPolygon, reallocating as needed. Returns possibly reallocated object.
requirements: mobj must be a valid LWMPOLY.
obj must be a valid LWPOLY.
Use returned pointer for subsequent access as address may change.

functions.name: lwpsurface_add_lwpoly
functions.description: Append an LWPOLY to a PolyhedralSurface, reallocating as needed. Returns possibly reallocated object.
requirements: mobj must be a valid LWPSURFACE.
obj must be a valid LWPOLY.
Use returned pointer for subsequent access as address may change.

functions.name: lwtin_add_lwtriangle
functions.description: Append an LWTRIANGLE to a TIN, reallocating as needed. Returns possibly reallocated object.
requirements: mobj must be a valid LWTIN.
obj must be a valid LWTRIANGLE.
Use returned pointer for subsequent access as address may change.

functions.name: lwcollection_concat_in_place
functions.description: Concatenate the geometries of col2 to col1 in place. Returns col1 (possibly reallocated).
requirements: col1 must be a valid, mutable collection; caller must use returned pointer as col1 may be reallocated.
col2 must be a valid collection.

functions.name: lwflags
functions.signature: lwflags_t lwflags(int hasz, int hasm, int geodetic);
functions.description: Build a flags bitmask representing Z/M presence and geodetic status.

functions.name: gserialized_get_lwflags
functions.description: Extract lwflags from a GSERIALIZED header.
requirements: g must point to a valid GSERIALIZED buffer with a proper header.

functions.name: gserialized_get_float_box_p
functions.description: Return a pointer to the embedded float bounding box in a GSERIALIZED, if present, and set ndims. Returns NULL if no bbox.
requirements: g must be a valid GSERIALIZED pointer.
If ndims is non-NULL, it will be assigned the number of bbox dimensions.

functions.name: gserialized_get_type
functions.description: Extract the geometry type code from a GSERIALIZED header.
requirements: g must point to a valid GSERIALIZED buffer.

functions.name: gserialized_max_header_size
functions.description: Return the maximum header size needed to read GSERIALIZED metadata (including optional bbox and type).

functions.name: gserialized_hash
functions.description: Compute a hash based on srid/type/geometry content, ignoring certain metadata like flags/optional boxes.
requirements: g must be a valid GSERIALIZED pointer.

functions.name: gserialized_get_srid
functions.description: Extract the SRID from a GSERIALIZED (packed into 3 bytes).
requirements: g must be a valid GSERIALIZED pointer.

functions.name: gserialized_set_srid
functions.description: Write the SRID into a GSERIALIZED (packed into 3 bytes).
requirements: g must be a valid, writable GSERIALIZED buffer.
srid should be within valid range; out-of-range behavior is library-defined.

functions.name: gserialized_is_empty
functions.description: Test if a GSERIALIZED is empty without full deserialization. Checks only top-level element count (nested empties may not be detected).
requirements: g must be a valid GSERIALIZED pointer.

functions.name: gserialized_has_bbox
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the GSERIALIZED payload has an embedded bounding box, zero otherwise.
requirements: gser must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GSERIALIZED buffer

functions.name: gserialized_has_z
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the GSERIALIZED payload has a Z ordinate, zero otherwise.
requirements: gser must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GSERIALIZED buffer

functions.name: gserialized_has_m
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the GSERIALIZED payload has an M ordinate, zero otherwise.
requirements: gser must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GSERIALIZED buffer

functions.name: gserialized_is_geodetic
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the GSERIALIZED represents geodetic (geography) coordinates, zero otherwise.
requirements: gser must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GSERIALIZED buffer

functions.name: gserialized_ndims
functions.description: Returns the number of dimensions in the geometry encoded in GSERIALIZED (2, 3, or 4).
requirements: gser must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GSERIALIZED buffer

functions.name: gserialized_cmp
functions.signature: extern int gserialized_cmp(const GSERIALIZED *g1, const GSERIALIZED *g2);
functions.description: Three-way comparison of two GSERIALIZED geometries: returns -1, 0, or 1. Equality is based on memcmp/size and may differ if one object lacks a bbox. Order uses a sortable key from object bounds centers.
requirements: g1 and g2 must be valid, non-NULL pointers to GSERIALIZED buffers

functions.name: gserialized_from_lwgeom
functions.description: Serializes an LWGEOM into a newly allocated GSERIALIZED. Non-point types get an embedded bbox. If size is non-NULL, it is set to the output size.
requirements: geom must be a valid pointer to an LWGEOM
Caller owns and must free the returned GSERIALIZED via the appropriate deallocator for this library context (unknown exact function from header)
size may be NULL; if not NULL it must be a valid pointer for output

functions.name: lwgeom_from_gserialized
functions.description: Deserializes a GSERIALIZED into a newly allocated LWGEOM with double-aligned coordinates suitable for direct reading via getPoint2d_cp-style accessors.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to GSERIALIZED data
Caller takes ownership of the returned LWGEOM and must free it with lwgeom_free()

functions.name: gserialized_get_gbox_p
functions.description: Fills box with the geometry bounding box. Uses header bbox if present, otherwise computes it. Returns LW_SUCCESS on success, LW_FAILURE on null/empty geometries.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL GSERIALIZED pointer
box must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to GBOX storage

functions.name: gserialized_fast_gbox_p
functions.description: Fills box with bbox if and only if one is present in the GSERIALIZED header. Returns LW_SUCCESS on success, LW_FAILURE otherwise.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL GSERIALIZED pointer
box must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to GBOX storage

functions.name: gserialized_set_gbox
functions.description: Ensures GSERIALIZED has the provided bounding box. May allocate and return a new GSERIALIZED if necessary. Caller must check if the returned pointer differs from input before freeing input.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL GSERIALIZED pointer
gbox must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GBOX with appropriate dimensionality
Caller must treat the return value as the new owner and avoid double-freeing input if a new object is returned

functions.name: gserialized_drop_gbox
functions.description: Returns a freshly allocated GSERIALIZED with any embedded bbox removed.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL GSERIALIZED pointer
Caller must use the returned pointer as the new object and free accordingly

functions.name: gserialized_get_version
functions.description: Returns the serialization version stored in the GSERIALIZED header.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL GSERIALIZED pointer

functions.name: gserialized_peek_first_point
functions.description: For POINTTYPE geometries, extracts the first point into out_point without full deserialization. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: g must be a valid, non-NULL GSERIALIZED pointer
out_point must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to POINT4D storage
Only succeeds for POINTTYPE; for other types, expect failure

functions.name: lwgeom_drop_bbox
functions.description: Removes bbox metadata from an LWGEOM; if a bbox exists but the geometry is not flagged as having one, the bbox memory will be released.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an LWGEOM

functions.name: lwgeom_drop_srid
functions.description: Clears the SRID from an LWGEOM.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an LWGEOM

functions.name: lwgeom_add_bbox
functions.description: Computes and attaches a bbox to the geometry if not already present. After call, lwgeom->bbox is NULL only if geometry is empty.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an LWGEOM

functions.name: lwgeom_refresh_bbox
functions.description: Recomputes the geometry bbox, dropping any current one and calculating a fresh bbox.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an LWGEOM

functions.name: lwgeom_add_bbox_deep
functions.description: Computes a bbox for the geometry and all sub-geometries if not already computed, potentially using gbox as working/output storage.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an LWGEOM
gbox must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a GBOX

functions.name: lwgeom_get_bbox
functions.description: Returns a non-NULL cached bbox if present, computing and caching it if necessary. Returns NULL for empty geometries.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an LWGEOM
Caller must not modify the returned GBOX

functions.name: lwgeom_is_collection
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the geometry is a collection type (has geoms/ngeoms members), zero otherwise.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL LWGEOM pointer

functions.name: lwgeom_is_unitary
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the geometry is unitary (not just a bag of sub-geometries), e.g., point/linestring/polygon/circularstring/compoundcurve/curvepolygon.
requirements: geom must be a valid, non-NULL LWGEOM pointer

functions.name: lwtype_is_unitary
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given lwtype code represents a unitary (non-collection) geometry type.
requirements: lwtype must be a valid LWTYPE numeric code

functions.name: lwgeom_has_patches
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the geometry type contains patches (surfaces composed of patches), zero otherwise.
requirements: geom must be a valid, non-NULL LWGEOM pointer

functions.name: lwgeom_has_rings
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the geometry type has rings enclosing an area (not a collection of areas), e.g., triangle, polygon, curvepolygon.
requirements: geom must be a valid, non-NULL LWGEOM pointer

functions.name: lwgeom_isfinite
functions.description: Checks if an LWGEOM has only finite coordinates (no NaN or Inf). Returns non-zero if all coordinates are finite.
requirements: lwgeom must be a valid, non-NULL LWGEOM pointer

functions.name: lwtype_is_collection
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the lwtype code represents a collection type.
requirements: type must be a valid lwtype numeric code (0-255)

functions.name: lwtype_get_collectiontype
functions.description: Given an lwtype, returns the homogeneous collection type that can hold it.
requirements: type must be a valid lwtype numeric code

functions.name: lwtype_name
functions.description: Returns the type name string (e.g., "Point", "LineString") associated with a type number.
requirements: type must be a valid lwtype numeric code
Returned pointer is to an internal/static string and must not be freed (inferred)

functions.name: lwtype_multitype
functions.description: Returns the multi-geometry lwtype corresponding to a base lwtype (e.g., Point -> MultiPoint).
requirements: type must be a valid lwtype numeric code

functions.name: getPoint4d
functions.signature: extern POINT4D getPoint4d(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Returns the nth point from a POINTARRAY as a POINT4D by value. Missing Z/M are set to 0 or NaN (implementation-defined by library).
requirements: pa must be a valid, non-NULL POINTARRAY
n must be a valid index within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint4d_p
functions.signature: extern int getPoint4d_p(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n, POINT4D *point);
functions.description: Writes the nth point from a POINTARRAY into point as POINT4D. Returns non-zero on success. Missing Z/M are set to defaults.
requirements: pa must be a valid, non-NULL POINTARRAY
point must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to POINT4D storage
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint3dz
functions.signature: extern POINT3DZ getPoint3dz(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Returns the nth point from a POINTARRAY as a POINT3DZ by value. If pa is 2D, z is set to 0 or NaN (implementation-defined).
requirements: pa must be a valid, non-NULL POINTARRAY
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint3dm
functions.signature: extern POINT3DM getPoint3dm(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Returns the nth point from a POINTARRAY as a POINT3DM by value. If pa lacks M, m is set to default (implementation-defined).
requirements: pa must be a valid, non-NULL POINTARRAY
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint3dz_p
functions.signature: extern int getPoint3dz_p(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n, POINT3DZ *point);
functions.description: Writes the nth point from a POINTARRAY into point as POINT3DZ. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: pa must be non-NULL
point must be non-NULL
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint3dm_p
functions.signature: extern int getPoint3dm_p(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n, POINT3DM *point);
functions.description: Writes the nth point from a POINTARRAY into point as POINT3DM. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: pa must be non-NULL
point must be non-NULL
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint2d
functions.signature: extern POINT2D getPoint2d(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Returns the nth point from a POINTARRAY as a POINT2D by value (Z/M, if present, are ignored).
requirements: pa must be a valid, non-NULL POINTARRAY
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: getPoint2d_p
functions.signature: extern int getPoint2d_p(const POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n, POINT2D *point);
functions.description: Writes the nth point from a POINTARRAY into point as POINT2D. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: pa must be non-NULL
point must be non-NULL
n must be within [0, pa->npoints)

functions.name: ptarray_set_point4d
functions.signature: extern void ptarray_set_point4d(POINTARRAY *pa, uint32_t n, const POINT4D *p4d);
functions.description: Sets point n in the POINTARRAY from the supplied POINT4D, extracting appropriate ordinates for the array dimensionality.
requirements: pa must be a valid, non-NULL POINTARRAY
p4d must be a valid, non-NULL POINT4D pointer
n must be a valid index [0, pa->npoints)
POINTARRAY dimensionality governs which ordinates from p4d are used

functions.name: ptarray_construct
functions.signature: extern POINTARRAY* ptarray_construct(char hasz, char hasm, uint32_t npoints);
functions.description: Allocates a new POINTARRAY with specified Z/M flags and sets npoints, without filling coordinates. Intended to be followed by ptarray_set_point4d calls.

data_types.description: A raw binary buffer containing tightly packed double-precision floating point ordinates for a sequence of points. The layout is: npoints consecutive points, each point having 2 to 4 doubles depending on dimensionality flags (XY, optionally Z if hasZ, optionally M if hasM). No headers or delimiters; just doubles in native endianness: [x0,y0,(z0),(m0), x1,y1,(z1),(m1), ...]. The consumer interprets the stride (2..4 doubles per point) from separate flags and the total length from npoints.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for packed double coordinate array buffers used by ptarray_construct_* fuzzer stubs.
# Layout: [x0, y0, (z0), (m0), x1, y1, (z1), (m1), ...] with 2..4 doubles per point in native endianness.
# The fuzz stubs determine hasZ/hasM and npoints and resize/fill their own buffers; however, providing
# semantically valid coordinate sequences increases exercise of downstream logic.

# We will emit a buffer that can plausibly serve multiple dimensionalities. The stubs will resize the
# buffer to the exact required size; when our buffer is shorter, it will be padded with zeros by resize;
# when longer, it will be truncated. Hence we aim to provide sufficiently rich data within a modest size.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

# Some interesting coordinate sets: geographic, projected, large/small magnitudes, rings, lines, duplicates.

def _ring(centerx: float, centery: float, r: float, n: int) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        ang = 2.0 * 3.141592653589793 * (i / max(1, n))
        pts.append((centerx + r * math_cos(ang), centery + r * math_sin(ang)))
    # close ring by repeating first if not already
    if n > 0:
        pts.append(pts[0])
    return pts

# Local fast trig without importing math repeatedly
from math import cos as math_cos, sin as math_sin


def _line(start: Tuple[float, float], dx: float, dy: float, n: int) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
    x, y = start
    pts = []
    for i in range(n):
        pts.append((x + dx * i, y + dy * i))
    return pts


def _grid(x0: float, y0: float, sx: float, sy: float, nx: int, ny: int) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
    pts = []
    for j in range(ny):
        for i in range(nx):
            pts.append((x0 + i * sx, y0 + j * sy))
    return pts


def _zigzag(x0: float, y0: float, step: float, n: int) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
    pts = []
    x, y = x0, y0
    for i in range(n):
        pts.append((x, y))
        if i % 2 == 0:
            x += step
        else:
            y += step
    return pts


def _random_points(rng: random.Random, n: int, domain: str) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
    pts = []
    if domain == "geographic":
        for _ in range(n):
            x = rng.uniform(-180.0, 180.0)
            y = rng.uniform(-90.0, 90.0)
            pts.append((x, y))
    elif domain == "projected":
        for _ in range(n):
            x = rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
            y = rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
            pts.append((x, y))
    else:  # generic
        for _ in range(n):
            x = rng.uniform(-1e3, 1e3)
            y = rng.uniform(-1e3, 1e3)
            pts.append((x, y))
    return pts


def _z_profile(kind: str, base: float, rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[float]:
    zs = []
    if kind == "flat":
        zs = [base] * n
    elif kind == "ramp":
        zs = [base + i * 1.0 for i in range(n)]
    elif kind == "wave":
        zs = [base + 10.0 * math_sin(i * 0.3) for i in range(n)]
    else:  # random
        zs = [rng.uniform(base - 100.0, base + 100.0) for _ in range(n)]
    return zs


def _m_profile(kind: str, base: float, rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[float]:
    ms = []
    if kind == "index":
        ms = [float(i) for i in range(n)]
    elif kind == "time":
        t = base
        for _ in range(n):
            ms.append(t)
            t += rng.uniform(0.1, 5.0)
    elif kind == "flat":
        ms = [base] * n
    else:  # random
        ms = [rng.uniform(base - 50.0, base + 50.0) for _ in range(n)]
    return ms


def _pack_points(points: List[Tuple[float, float]], hasz: bool, hasm: bool,
                 zs: List[float] | None, ms: List[float] | None) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    n = len(points)
    for i in range(n):
        x, y = points[i]
        out += struct.pack('=d', x)
        out += struct.pack('=d', y)
        if hasz:
            z = 0.0 if zs is None else zs[i]
            out += struct.pack('=d', z)
        if hasm:
            m = 0.0 if ms is None else ms[i]
            out += struct.pack('=d', m)
    return bytes(out)


def _build_suite(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Randomly choose dimensionality hints to bias data content; the stub decides actual dims.
    hasz = rng.choice([False, True])
    hasm = rng.choice([False, True])

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Small geographic ring (tests closedness and bbox)
    ring_n = rng.randint(4, 12)
    ring_pts = _ring(rng.uniform(-10, 10), rng.uniform(-10, 10), rng.uniform(0.1, 5.0), ring_n)
    zs = _z_profile(rng.choice(["flat", "ramp", "wave", "random"]), rng.uniform(0, 100), rng, len(ring_pts)) if hasz else None
    ms = _m_profile(rng.choice(["index", "time", "flat", "random"]), rng.uniform(0, 1000), rng, len(ring_pts)) if hasm else None
    chunks.append(_pack_points(ring_pts, hasz, hasm, zs, ms))

    # 2) Polyline with duplicates and small gaps (tests allow_duplicates, gap_tolerance)
    line_pts = _line((rng.uniform(-100, 100), rng.uniform(-100, 100)), rng.uniform(0.5, 5.0), rng.uniform(0.5, 5.0), rng.randint(2, 20))
    # introduce a duplicate endpoint occasionally
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and line_pts:
        line_pts.insert(len(line_pts)//2, line_pts[max(0, len(line_pts)//2 - 1)])
    zs = _z_profile(rng.choice(["flat", "ramp", "random"]), rng.uniform(-50, 50), rng, len(line_pts)) if hasz else None
    ms = _m_profile(rng.choice(["index", "random"]), rng.uniform(0, 10), rng, len(line_pts)) if hasm else None
    chunks.append(_pack_points(line_pts, hasz, hasm, zs, ms))

    # 3) Grid cluster (tests closest vertex/segment and bbox)
    gx = rng.randint(2, 6)
    gy = rng.randint(2, 6)
    grid_pts = _grid(rng.uniform(-1000, 1000), rng.uniform(-1000, 1000), rng.uniform(1, 100), rng.uniform(1, 100), gx, gy)
    zs = _z_profile("flat", rng.uniform(-10, 10), rng, len(grid_pts)) if hasz else None
    ms = _m_profile("index", 0.0, rng, len(grid_pts)) if hasm else None
    chunks.append(_pack_points(grid_pts, hasz, hasm, zs, ms))

    # 4) Zigzag short path
    zz_pts = _zigzag(rng.uniform(-50, 50), rng.uniform(-50, 50), rng.uniform(0.1, 10.0), rng.randint(3, 15))
    zs = _z_profile("wave", rng.uniform(0, 20), rng, len(zz_pts)) if hasz else None
    ms = _m_profile("time", rng.uniform(0, 100), rng, len(zz_pts)) if hasm else None
    chunks.append(_pack_points(zz_pts, hasz, hasm, zs, ms))

    # 5) Random scatter in projected or geographic space
    domain = rng.choice(["geographic", "projected", "generic"])
    rp_n = rng.randint(1, 32)
    rp_pts = _random_points(rng, rp_n, domain)
    zs = _z_profile(rng.choice(["random", "flat"]), rng.uniform(-200, 200), rng, len(rp_pts)) if hasz else None
    ms = _m_profile(rng.choice(["random", "index"]), rng.uniform(-100, 100), rng, len(rp_pts)) if hasm else None
    chunks.append(_pack_points(rp_pts, hasz, hasm, zs, ms))

    buf = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(buf) > MAX_BYTES:
        buf = buf[:MAX_BYTES]
    return buf


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build one or two suites and concatenate to mix patterns
    buf = _build_suite(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        buf2 = _build_suite(rng)
        # Keep within cap
        remaining = MAX_BYTES - len(buf)
        buf += buf2[:max(0, remaining)]
    # Ensure non-empty; if empty, add a single XY point at origin
    if not buf:
        buf = struct.pack('=dd', 0.0, 0.0)
    return buf
